wy_lower_blacktail_butte.blurb: Lower Blacktail Butte is the lowest wall on Blacktail Butte in Grand Teton National Park, just above the trailhead lot near Moose. It holds about sixteen climbs, mostly bolted sport lines and a couple of top ropes, with a single boulder problem. Grades start around 5.10 and pile up in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, with the bulk at 5.12. The limestone is technical, polished and slick, so it suits strong leaders rather than beginners. It is the nearest climbing to the car, which makes it handy for a short session, and a trail around the side reaches the cliff top for anchors.

wy_tunnel_the.blurb: The Tunnel is a big slab leaning against the southeast corner of the Hightower wall on Reese Mountain, in the Laramie Range of southeast Wyoming. Most of its sixteen climbs are traditional lines, with two bolted routes and one aid project, and the difficulty runs from 5.8 up to 5.11. Roughly half sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate trad and slab terrain. The top bolted line here is a two-pitch outing. To get there, circle the base of the Hightower wall from its southwest corner until the slab appears.

_expect.name: La Cueva de la Cabra (AKA The Goat Cave)

wy_la_cueva_de_la_cabra_aka_the_goat_cav.blurb: The Goat Cave is a small limestone cave crag along the highway south of Jackson, overlooking the Snake River. All sixteen climbs are sport routes, from 5.9 to 5.13, though most are 5.12 and 5.13 with a handful of 5.11s, so it favours climbers working harder grades. It faces southeast and falls into shade by mid-afternoon in summer, and the routes are best when the rock is dry. Some of the older bolts are reportedly tired, and rock on the approach is loose, so move carefully. The walk from the roadside pullout takes about a quarter hour.

wy_04_precious_metals_wall.blurb: Precious Metals Wall is the upper tier of the middle section of the Periodic Table, a large limestone fin in Swift Creek Canyon near Jackson Hole. Fifteen of its sixteen climbs are sport routes, almost all between 5.11 and 5.12 with one easier 5.10, plus a single trad line. The stone is vertical and featured, with pockets and crimps on grey, blue and white streaks, and it is regarded as the best-quality rock on the formation. The wall faces west, so mornings are shaded and the sun arrives in the afternoon. Expect a long, steep hike in with a short fixed-line section.

wy_3_saddle_tramp.blurb: Saddle Tramp is the third and last section of the Central crag at Wild Iris, the high-elevation sport area outside Lander, at roughly 8,900 feet. All sixteen routes are bolted, with grades running from 5.7 through 5.12 and the majority in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it works well for solid intermediates. It has a reputation for a good concentration of quality lines, and the cliff runs on from the neighbouring Claim Jumper section. Reach it by branching off the main dirt road trails; the main path leads to the neighbouring section first.

wy_eagle_rock.blurb: Eagle Rock is an isolated granite crag on Telephone Road, in the Vedauwoo area of the Laramie region. Of its sixteen climbs, fourteen are traditional routes and two are boulder problems, with trad grades from 5.7 up to 5.12 and the heaviest cluster around 5.9 to 5.11. The granite is notably clean and the crag has several prominent features, a quieter alternative to the busier Vedauwoo formations. Bring a full trad rack. The drive in follows Telephone Road past a four-way junction, and you can park close to the base of the rock.

wy_full_charge_crag.blurb: Full Charge Crag is the farthest-right crag of the Lake Point sector in Ten Sleep Canyon, sitting on towers beside a triple bulge on the down-canyon end. All sixteen routes are sport climbs, from 5.9 to 5.11, with most in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, a good fit for climbers stepping up in grade. Reach it by taking the main Lake Point trail and then heading right across two talus slopes. The sector as a whole has compact rock with juggy holds, pillars and horizontal pocket lines, and its tree-filtered afternoon light keeps temperatures workable.
